shopify.text: Native. Free themes by Shopify and paid themes from third parties in the Theme Store (hundreds; paid examples $100 to $420); Basic, Grow and Advanced stores can add up to 20 themes, Plus up to 100, Starter only Spotlight.

gap: Built since the last read (D241 to D287, docs/theme-store.md, docs/theme-prices.md): the theme store at /themes with a page per theme, a full-screen preview on the theme's own demo content (D275, D276) and the inert, noindex public preview; presets (D256); Add to my themes and Try it in your store install a theme without going live (D248); applying copies pictures into the store's library, keeps its own pages and products and puts the look before away in the theme library (D241, D244); switching keeps every install (theme-installs.int.test.ts, signed-in theme-switch.spec.ts through every launch theme and back with no content changed); unpublish and archive take a theme out of every list (design-presets.int.test.ts); updates reach installs that follow them (on by default, the owner can switch it off), with What's new and undo (D245). Paid themes (D286): a price per currency, shown on the cards, the theme page and before the button that pays; nothing is charged before the store goes live with it; invoiced through Kaizena Flow's Stripe billing and settled by the billing webhook. Still short: (1) the collection of a premium theme's invoice is held only against the repository's stand-in for Stripe (theme-prices.int.test.ts); no premium theme has been invoiced and paid in Stripe's test mode on a real store, the precedent D173, D174 and D239 hold rows to. Criteria restated on 2026-10-19: the first criterion asked that a store owner publish a whole theme to a marketplace, which is not part of Shopify's theme store (themes there come from Shopify and from designers it admits); themes from outside designers are scored in platform.themes-and-templates-marketplace.
criteria: Whole themes (look settings, header, footer, product layout and presets) are listed in a theme store with a page each, and any store previews one, inert and without saving, before using it.
Using a theme copies it into the store (pictures included) without touching the store's products or pages, and the look before stays in the store's theme library.
A platform admin can unpublish or archive a theme, and it leaves every list and choice at once.
A store holds several themes and switches the live one without losing the others; a test covers the switch.

A theme is free or paid; a paid theme's price is shown before anything is paid, the store pays once, and the payment is collected and settled through the platform's billing (proven against Stripe in test mode, not only a stand-in).

shopify.text: Native. Sections and blocks in the theme editor: up to 25 sections and 1,250 blocks per template, nested blocks up to eight levels where the theme supports them.

gap: Caveat, not a gap in the editor: a page is rows of columns of blocks, with one more level where a column holds a Columns component (D294, one level deep) or an FAQ answer holds components (D208); at most 50 rows and 100 blocks a page (`ROWS_MAX`, `BLOCKS_MAX` in `src/lib/page-content.ts`), where Shopify allows 25 sections, 1,250 blocks and up to eight nested levels per template. Built since the first read: undo, redo and page versions (D305), find and replace (D307), words edited in place on the canvas and the live site (D191 to D193).
criteria: Rows, columns and blocks are added from the palette and moved by dragging, and the canvas draws the page as the site does.
Every row, column and block takes spacing, border, background, width and responsive settings from its settings dialog.
A page over the row or block cap is refused with a plain message when saved.
Saved and global parts can be reused across pages, and a change to a global part is written to every page that uses it.

shopify.text: Native.

criteria: A store chooses which of its pages draws the cart, checkout, order, account, sign-in, wishlist, subscription, deliveries, cookies, blog, search, 404, category and tag places, each with a starter page.
A working page keeps the shop's own component on its route, and a route draws the standard page when none is chosen.
Product pages use a layout chosen by product, category, tag or store, else the default layout.
Cart, checkout and order come apart into pieces that draw nothing when they have nothing to show.

shopify.text: Native.

criteria: A store's colours (light and dark sets), fonts, buttons, corners, content width and header style are one theme, edited in one place and applied to every page without fixed colours.
Colour pairs below WCAG AA contrast are warned about in the editor.
A theme can be saved, applied and deleted, and the visitor's light or dark choice follows the theme.

feature: Custom pages and front page selection

shopify.text: Native.

criteria: An owner builds a page in the page builder, publishes it at its own address in every market, and links it from menus by address.
One page can be the store's front page and one its All products page; their own addresses redirect to the place.
A page is duplicated as an unpublished draft, and a published page's address moves only on publish, leaving a redirect.
The AI page studio builds a page as a draft from an interview.

shopify.text: Native. Several blogs per store; comments off, held for moderation or auto-published, with a spam filter; an Atom feed generated for every blog at the blog's address with .atom appended.

gap: Articles are pages of type `article` built in the full page builder (D57), with a free-text author name, categories and tags, `Article` JSON-LD and one `/blog` per store (a page role, D112). Verified 2026-10-25: no second blog, no author records, no comments, and no RSS or Atom route.
criteria: A store can have several blogs, each with its own address, title, listing page and sitemap entries.
Each blog has a feed (Atom or RSS) at a stable address, listing published articles with title, summary, date and author; a test parses it.
Authors are records (name, picture, short text, link) chosen on an article and shown on it and in its JSON-LD.
Visitors can comment on an article when the blog allows it; comments are held for moderation, checked for spam, and shown only when approved, with consent and erasure rules honoured.

shopify.text: Native. Menus with up to two levels of drop-down under a top item (three in all), each menu up to 10,000 items and 1,000 menus per store; mega menus are theme-dependent.

criteria: An owner builds named menus of links to pages, products, categories, tags, articles, the site's own links or any address, nested to three levels by dragging.
A top link can be a mega menu with columns and pictures, drawn across the header's width; the phone's drawer shows nested links.
A menu is shown wherever it is chosen (header, footer or a menu block) and moves between stores with the store copy.

shopify.text: Native.

criteria: A store builds its header and footer in the page builder from site parts and menus, with an overlay header over pages that start with a background.
A store footer always carries the business details, the cookies link and the withdrawal link, which cannot be hidden on phones (D153); a layout without them is refused.
Announcement bars and other overlays are modal rows (D121), and a header or footer can be A/B tested.

shopify.text: Native.

gap: Owner CSS for a page and for the whole site, checked by `cssProblem()` (D100), also typed on the live page beside Edit text and kept as a version (D306), a sandboxed HTML block (`HtmlFrame`) and consent-gated head and body snippets (D61, only on a store's own host). No templating language, no file editing, no custom sections or JavaScript of the owner's own in the page. Whether to offer one is a security and product decision, not a missing form.
criteria: Decision recorded: either owners get a safe extension surface (a sandboxed templating or component language) or the row is declared out of scope with the reason.

If built: an owner's custom section is validated, sandboxed (no script access to cookies, storage or the admin) and rendered through the same page and theme system, with a test that a hostile section cannot read other stores' data.
A change to custom code is versioned and revertible, and goes through the consent rules for any script it loads.

shopify.text: Native. The theme editor's font library holds Monotype fonts, Google Fonts and web-safe fonts; the pages read say nothing of uploading own font files (third-party guides say that needs the code editor).

gap: Caveat: no upload of an owner's own font files; about 1,800 Google families are self-hosted. Shopify's picker also offers licensed Monotype fonts, which Kaizen does not. A family with no stylesheet is served empty so a streamed page never breaks (D316, `e2e/missing-font.spec.ts`).
criteria: A store chooses a heading and a body font from the catalogue; the family is downloaded once and served from Kaizen, never from Google.
A block can take its own font, installed before it is used.

shopify.text: Native.

criteria: Owners choose entrance, hover, scroll and background effects from curated lists; owner data never becomes CSS or script.
All content is present without JavaScript, with reduced motion and after the failsafe; the first row never starts transparent.
A 'Make my page cool' plan is validated in code and falls back to rules without AI.

shopify.text: Native. Responsive themes; the theme editor has a mobile preview toggle (desktop and mobile; the page read names no tablet toggle and no per-device settings).

criteria: The builder has a device toggle (computer, tablet, phone) that redraws the canvas at that width.
Spacing, visibility, alignment, order and column counts can be set per device on rows, columns and blocks, and the site honours them with CSS only, so the first paint is right.
A setting made for phones does not change the computer view; a test renders both.

history.why: D179 (docs/responsive-editing.md, phases 1 to 4) shipped after the last re-read. Read src/lib/responsive.ts, src/lib/part-css.ts, src/lib/breakpoints.ts, src/lib/visibility.ts and src/components/admin/responsive-edit.tsx: the builder's responsive mode draws the canvas at Small, Medium, Large and Extra large (the store's own widths, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+R); spacing, typography and alignment, columns, column order per line, widths and visibility (hideAt) are set per size on rows, columns and blocks in PartBase.at and written as CSS rules only (media queries on the site, container queries on the canvas), so the first paint is right. Held by responsive.test.ts (a medium or small value is written inside its media query and the base is untouched), responsive-edit.test.ts, visibility.test.ts, and the browser tests text-colour.spec.ts and gallery.spec.ts (a value set for Small changes the phone and not the computer), responsive-parity.spec.ts (old pages unchanged) and visibility.spec.ts; all passed on 2026-10-19 (pnpm test, and the e2e suite against a production build).

shopify.text: Native. Content > Files: images, videos and other files with search, size, type and 'Used in' filters, alt text and multi-delete; images up to 20 MB, videos up to 1 GB, 200 files per upload.

criteria: Every uploaded picture and video is registered once per store; the library shows where each is used and deletes the file from storage.
Search finds a file by name alone and pictures by their alt texts in every language, with AI alt texts that never overwrite staff's.
The site shows library alt texts where a picture has none of its own.
Files from before compressing was measured are offered Compress, one or all, in the browser, and every editable use moves to the smaller file (D213).

feature: Page speed: CDN, image optimisation, report

shopify.text: Native. Online store speed report in the admin: Lighthouse scores of the home page and the highest-traffic collection and product pages combined into one score, compared with similar stores; Shopify serves themes and images from its CDN.

criteria: A speed report in the store admin shows lab scores (or measured Core Web Vitals) for the front page and a top product and category page, with the date of the run and what to fix.
Pictures are served in a modern format at the visitor's device size with `srcset`, and a test checks the markup of a product card and a page picture.
A performance budget (page weight, largest image, time to first byte) is checked in CI for the demo store's home and product pages.
The report says what it cannot measure, never a score from nothing.

history.why: Wave 7 unit B (D336): product cards, content grid tiles, picture components and the product gallery offer the library's two files (WebP or AVIF from upload, 480 and up to 1600 px) by width with sizes from the columns (SizedPicture, picture-sizes.test.ts reads the markup of a card and a picture component). Analytics -> Speed shows measured Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS, TTFB) per kind of page (front page, product, category and tag, lists, other) and screen at the 75th percentile over 28 days, with the period, the last sample, Google's ratings and what to fix first, a figure under 20 page loads left out with its count, and what it cannot measure (lab runs not run); speed.test.ts, speed-view.test.ts and analytics-speed.int.test.ts hold it. e2e/performance.spec.ts holds page weight, the largest picture and the first byte of the demo store's front and product page on a phone.

shopify.text: Native.

gap: Caveat: no list of returns in My account (a withdrawal or return is reached from the order page and its email, D153). Built since the first read: saved addresses, up to 20 with a default for shipping and one for billing (D304, `src/server/customer-addresses.ts`), *Your orders* with search and paging (D304 J2, `account/orders`), reviews to write (D301), the data export (D162) and support conversations (D216). Account depth is its own row in the customers domain.
criteria: A shopper signs in with an emailed code or a password, sees orders, details, subscriptions and weekly deliveries, and can delete the account.
The account page is a page-builder role, so its layout and theme follow the store's.
Company, bonus and referral pages appear only where the store uses them.
Sign-in answers the same whether or not an address has an account.

shopify.text: Native (Rollouts, Basic and above): schedule theme changes and A/B test them against the current theme on real traffic, judged by conversions only; market-specific targeting on Advanced and Plus.

criteria: An owner tests a page, a row or block of it, the header, footer, a product layout, a modal or a working page, with a split of visitors who accepted statistics.
Results are computed on read with the verdict only after the minimum, a guardrail stops a harmful test and emails the owners, and the winner is applied by the owner.
A test is scheduled to start by itself, and no price, shipping or legal page is ever tested.

shopify.text: Native.

gap: Pages, headers, footers and themes have draft and published only: no publish or unpublish time on `commerce.pages` and no job that publishes content or switches a look by itself (verified 2026-10-25). Scheduling exists elsewhere: A/B tests start by themselves (`experiments.scheduled_start`, `runExperimentJobs()`), campaigns and discount codes have start and end times, broadcasts can be scheduled (D297), and a theme install that follows updates is updated by the five-minute job (D245); none of these is a scheduled page, header, footer or theme change with an automatic revert.
criteria: A page, header, footer or theme change can be scheduled for a date and time in the store's time zone and goes live by itself from a job, with nobody signed in.
An optional end time puts the previous published version back by itself.
The schedule, its result and any failure show in the page list and the audit log; a failed start leaves the page as it was.
A scheduled change to a page in a running A/B test is refused at scheduling time, as publishing is.

shopify.text: Native. Preview links for any added theme (visitor previews expire after 2 days, merchant previews after 30) and a finite Timeline of older versions of theme files in the code editor.

gap: Built (D305): every save, publish, text edit and CSS edit on the live site keeps a version (`keepVersion()` in `src/server/page-versions.ts`, the newest 50 per page, `VERSIONS_KEPT`, with who and when), listed in the builder's Versions and taken back as unsaved changes, never over the published page; the builder has undo and redo (buttons and keys). Missing: (1) a preview link an outsider opens without signing in (expiring, revocable, noindex): the signed tokens that exist open one replicator job's draft (`replicate-token.ts`, D150) or one page's draft for the AI manager's look for ten minutes (`/admin/account/look/{page}`, D310), and neither is offered to owners to share; (2) versions of the store's own theme settings: a theme's published versions (D241) and the look before an update (`theme_install_updates`, D245) are kept, but each save of the live look in Design settings or the builder's Theme tab is not.
criteria: Each publish (and each theme save) keeps a revision with author and time, and the last N are listed.
An owner restores a revision as the new draft, never silently over the published page.
The builder has undo and redo for the current session.
A preview link opens an unpublished page or theme without signing in, expires, can be revoked, is noindex and exposes nothing else (token like `replicate-token.ts`).

shopify.text: Native.

criteria: Every page, article and product has a title and description with length advice, a noindex switch (left out of the sitemap too) and its own address.
A page's changed address redirects the old one for good.
A store's home title and description are per language, and verification codes for search consoles can be set.

shopify.text: Native. sitemap.xml is generated for products with their primary image, pages, collections and blog posts; languages are added for each domain.

gap: Evidence debt, narrower now: hreflang alternates and x-default are asserted (`src/server/seo.int.test.ts` for categories and tags, `e2e/smoke.spec.ts` for the store sitemap), but no test asserts the `image:image` picture entries `storeSitemap()` writes (`src/server/seo.ts`).
criteria: Each store has a sitemap listing its products, pages and articles in every market with hreflang alternates, x-default and picture entries, linked from the platform's sitemap index.
A hidden store, a noindex page and a page chosen for a working role are left out.

shopify.text: Native, theme-dependent: themes emit schema.org JSON-LD through the structured_data Liquid filter (Product, or ProductGroup with variants); it is not a platform setting.

criteria: Product pages carry Product JSON-LD with price, availability, brand, picture, shipping and return policy (the store's own 14-day or longer policy, D153); variants group under one product.
Pages carry breadcrumbs and articles carry Article data; the store carries its business node.
Downloads are always in stock with no shipping or returns.

shopify.text: Native via the theme: a default robots.txt, customised by adding robots.txt.liquid in the code editor (add or remove rules, host-specific rules, extra sitemaps).

criteria: The platform's robots.txt lists each open store's rules under its address; an owner adds crawler rules that are parsed and refused with the line number when unreadable.
AI assistants and AI training have their own switches, and a page can be closed to AI crawlers one by one.
A hidden store is left out of the sitemap index and llms.txt and its pages ask not to be indexed.

shopify.text: Native. Content > Menus > URL redirects: create manually, import and export CSV, up to 100,000 redirects (Plus 20,000,000); the page read does not describe automatic prompts on handle changes.

criteria: Changing the address of a product, category, tag or article leaves a permanent redirect from the old one, as pages do now, and a later page taking that address replaces it.
An owner adds, edits, deletes and searches manual redirects from a path to a path or address, scoped to the store.
CSV import and export with validation: loops, chains, duplicates and external hosts are reported per line; an import is a resumable job.
A 404 report lists the most requested missing paths, each with a one-click redirect.

history.why: D168 (wave 2, second run, docs/wave-2-redirects.md). Read the code and ran the cited tests on a fresh database: unit and PGlite (114 files, 2183 tests), integration (9 files, 128 tests: redirects, redirect-resolve, redirect-import, not-found, term-seo, seo, store-translate, redirect-tools, taxonomy) and, on a production build, e2e redirects, redirects-admin, terms and smoke (28 passed). (1) A rename of a product that was live, of a category or of a tag leaves an automatic redirect from commerce.redirects through database triggers (PGlite: three renames leave three rows, a taken address replaces the automatic one, swaps end consistent) and the old address answers 308 to the current one in the same market (redirect-resolve.int.test.ts, e2e/redirects.spec.ts); pages and articles keep page_redirects (commerce.test.ts). (2) Manual redirects are added, edited, deleted and searched through src/server/redirects.ts, scoped by store id, refused for a live source, a working page, another website and a loop, capped at 100,000, one transaction with the audit entry. (3) CSV import is a D165 job (redirect_import: per-line dry run with a finding code for loops, chains, duplicates and external hosts, chunked and resumable apply, each line judged again at write time) and export imports back unchanged (redirect-import.int.test.ts). (4) The 404 report (commerce.not_found_hits, address and day and counts only) lists addresses by count over 7, 30 or 90 days with up to three suggested targets found in code and a one-click manual redirect, otherwise a short form (not-found.int.test.ts, e2e). Caveats, so the rating is not read wider than it is: the signed-in admin screens (manager, import, export, report) are held by renderToString views and by the integration tests of the functions their actions call, not by an end-to-end test, because the repository has no signed-in admin fixture (e2e/redirects-admin.spec.ts holds the signed-out refusals only); a target on another website is refused as an error, narrower than Shopify; the 404 counts and a redirect's hits are lower bounds (a miss is recorded in the cached lookup's fill, at most about once a second per address and instance, so a very busy address is under-counted and the order of two very busy addresses is approximate), and robots are told apart only for addresses with no country, which the proxy sees; the Location header is sent twice on the first on-demand render of a redirect (browsers accept it).

shopify.text: Native. Logo and favicon in theme settings; a favicon needs the Basic plan or higher (16x16 or 32x32 px, larger images reduced to 32).

criteria: A store uploads logos (with a variant for dark backgrounds) and an icon; the browser makes a 64 and a 512 pixel PNG, and every layout links them.
/favicon.ico redirects to the site's icon, and Kaizen's icon is the default.
A share image is used when a page has none of its own.

shopify.text: Native.

criteria: A row set as a modal opens from a link, hash, element class, timer or exit intent; it opens by itself at most once per page view, never over another modal or on working pages.
Frequency memory is a preferences item written only after consent, and without consent nothing is stored.
Focus is trapped and returned, Escape closes it, and a sign-up form inside works.

feature: Signup and contact forms feeding customers and consent

shopify.text: Native.

gap: D295: a confirmed newsletter sign-up feeds the store's subscriber list with consent (words, time, source, language, confirmation time), unsubscribes by the subscriber's own link or one-click, and is in the person's export and erasure. D304 J3: a form's tags are put on the confirmed address as customer tags (`tagFromForm()`), which segments select (`kind: 'tag'`, D296), held by `signup-codes.int.test.ts` and `segments.int.test.ts`. Still missing: contact messages in an admin inbox: the email form only emails its recipients and counts a row in `form_submissions` (`src/server/forms.ts`), with no status and no link to the customer with that address (the support inbox, D216, takes chat conversations and, since D332, emails to the desk's address, but not form messages, and on purpose never ties an email to a customer by its address, so criterion 3 is still unmet).
criteria: A confirmed newsletter sign-up creates or updates a subscriber (store, email, source form, consent text and time, language, double opt-in time), not only an email to the owner.
A subscriber unsubscribes by a signed link, the record shows it, and it can be exported and erased.
A contact message appears in an admin inbox with a status and links to the customer with the same email.
A form can tag its subscribers, and tags are selectable in segments.

shopify.text: Native via the Translate & Adapt app: products, collections, blog posts, policies and pages; automatic translation for at most two languages, manual translation without a limit, policies never automatic.

gap: Caveat: a language may also have a domain of its own (D313). Category and tag names and descriptions are translatable since D319 (`terms.texts`, read through `termTextFor()`, in the translation worklist). Merged on 2026-10-26 (README rule 8): `international.multi-language-storefront-and-ai-translation` was the same Shopify feature (rated full); its criteria and evidence are here.
criteria: A page is built once in the store's main language with texts in other languages over it; the site shows the shopper's language with hreflang alternates.
A language and a currency are chosen apart from the country, and the store's languages come from `store.localization`.
A whole store is translated with AI from one worklist, a person reads every text before it is saved, and legal pages start unticked.
Interface text of added languages is translated into data and read key by key, with English as the fallback.
Every AI translation passes validation (shape, length, claims filter), and product, page and store texts fall back to the main language when no translation exists.

feature: Custom data rendered in the theme

shopify.text: Native. Metafields connect to theme settings through dynamic sources in the theme editor (Text and Rich text settings; up to 20 metafields per template).

criteria: Owners define field groups with location rules and conditional logic for products, variants, categories, tags, pages, articles and the store, and values are shown only when the owner makes them public.
A heading, rich text, image or button block can be bound to a field, and a repeater draws as cards, a list or a grid.
A field can be a listing filter, part of search and a fact for the chat agent.

shopify.text: Native, narrow: a cookie banner governing Shopify's own cookies and pixels, set up automatically for UK and EEA visitors with active markets there; third-party trackers need a separate banner, and the page names no consent log or cookie scan.

gap: Caveat: the Consent Mode v2 signals sent by `consent-manager.tsx` are read from the code and held by no test. Merged on 2026-10-26 (README rule 8): `international.cookie-consent-banner-and-api` was the same Shopify feature (rated full); its criteria and evidence are here.
criteria: A store with only necessary cookies shows no banner; one with a tracking tool asks first, loads the tool only after consent and logs each choice for 12 months.
Every cookie or storage item is declared with category and purpose, and the cookies page lists what the latest scan found.
A store's own code runs only after consent unless it is necessary.
A site re-asks when the categories it uses change; each choice is logged through `/api/consent` (`commerce.consents`).

shopify.text: Native. Sidekick adjusts a theme from a description and creates custom blocks in any Theme Store theme; AI generates a whole store from a description of what to sell.

gap: Built since the last read (D308 to D310): the AI manager builds and edits page drafts (`build_page`, `edit_page`; built after the answer by `runPageJobs()`, `publish_page` gated), makes menus of the store's own links only (`save_menu`, gated while a menu is shown), chooses the standard header's and footer's menus and logo (`set_header_footer`, gated), adds, previews and makes a theme or preset live (`add_theme`, `try_theme`, `make_theme_live`, gated, the charge kept with the approval), sets the store's details, countries, languages, currencies and shipping (setup tools, at once while the store is being set up), and looks at what it built (`look_at_page`, `look_at_store`); the page studio (D92), the replicator (D150) and a theme's starting content (D275) remain. Since D330 criterion 1 holds: `design_look` designs a look of the store's own from a description (a few brand colours, fonts and Design settings' named choices, both palettes worked out by `designedTheme()` and refused under 4.5:1 by `themeWarnings()`), adds it to the theme library not live, and it reaches visitors only through the gated `make_theme_live`. Still short: (1) no custom header or footer layout from AI, only the standard one's menus and logo (criterion 2); (2) no single flow from one description to theme, front page, pages and menus as drafts: the owner, or a plan the owner approves (D309), drives it tool by tool.
criteria: The AI manager can propose a theme change (colours, fonts, buttons) from a description as a gated change the owner approves, with contrast warnings applied.
The AI can draft a header, footer and menus as drafts, linking only to the store's real pages.
A store setup from one description produces theme, front page, a few pages and menus as drafts for the owner to read; nothing is published without a yes.
Every AI text passes the claims filter and the feature falls back with a plain message when no model is set.

history.why: Read Shopify's Winter '26 edition page (Sidekick edits themes and builds blocks; AI generates a whole store) and the code: Kaizen's AI builds page drafts only, with no AI path to the theme, header, footer or menus and no whole-store generation. The first report's own caveat ('not whole-store redesigns') now matters because Shopify's claim is store-wide.

shopify.text: Native. Private mode hides every page from visitors and search engines behind a customisable password landing page (password header, footer and email sign-up sections); new stores start private.

gap: A store whose setup is not finished (or with `seo.hidden`) is noindexed and left out of sitemaps, llms.txt and feeds, but anyone with the address can view it; a suspended or closed store is a 404 (D171) and a store with its shop off is a website (D178), neither a private mode. No password, no coming-soon page built in the builder, no unlock cookie, and no way to put an open store back in private mode (verified 2026-10-25: no such column, setting or route).
criteria: An owner switches a store to private mode with a password; visitors see a landing page built in the page builder until they enter it, and the unlock cookie is declared necessary in `KNOWN_COOKIES`.
In private mode no page, sitemap, llms.txt or feed lists the store, crawlers get noindex and disallow, and signed-in staff preview without the password.
An owner can re-hide an open store; the change is in the audit log, and orders already placed keep working (webhooks, order pages).
A store that has not finished setup is private by default.

history.why: The first report's recheck: unopened stores are viewable by address, noindexed and left out of sitemaps; there is still no password or landing page.

shopify.text: Native, as a theme requirement: Theme Store themes need a minimum average Lighthouse accessibility score of 90 over the home, product, collection and cart pages; no merchant-facing accessibility checker is described.

gap: All four criteria are built and tested; Partial because the independent audit is bucket D and the checkout's own markup and Stripe's form are not scanned. `e2e/a11y.spec.ts` (axe up to `wcag22aa`, light and dark, serious and critical fail) covers the signed-out pages CI reaches, and since PSI ACC-01 `e2e/signed-in/a11y.spec.ts` scans the owner's and platform admin's most-used pages and the skip link; the builder's Checks tab (`src/lib/page-a11y.ts`: alt text, empty links and buttons, heading order, contrast with opacity, placeholders, translations) links each issue to its block; `savePage()` asks before publishing with a blocking issue and records the choice (`page.published_with_issues`); the statement is generated from facts the site holds and flagged for review. Missing: (1) the independent audit (bucket D); (2) the checkout page itself: the demo store takes no payments, so `a11y.spec.ts`'s checkout test follows the redirect to the cart and scans that, and `csp.spec.ts` reads headers only, so the address, delivery choice, terms tick box and pay button are scanned by nobody, nor is Stripe's form, and the manual run is recorded nowhere (docs/pci.md); (3) the checker reads a page's own content only (owner CSS and a picture behind text are not read) and does not notice a translation made stale by a later edit.
criteria: An automated WCAG check (axe or equivalent) runs in CI over the storefront's front, product, cart, order, account (signed out) and withdraw pages and the checkout in the states reachable without a payment session, in light and dark, and fails on serious or critical violations. The payment form is checked by hand and recorded.
The page builder lists issues in a page's draft: pictures without alt text, heading order, empty links or buttons, text over a background below 4.5:1, with a link to the block.
Publishing a page with an unresolved blocking issue shows a warning and records the owner's choice.
An accessibility statement can be generated from facts the site holds, flagged for review.
